prompt: A car accelerates uniformly from $4.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ to $10.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ in $3.0\ \text{s}$. What is the displacement of the car in this time?
markscheme: **C.** For uniform acceleration the average velocity is $\tfrac{4.0 + 10.0}{2} = 7.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, so $s = 7.0 \times 3.0 = 21\ \text{m}$.

A car travelling at 25 m s⁻¹ brakes uniformly and stops in 40 m.

**(a)** Calculate its deceleration. **[2]**

**(b)** Calculate the time taken to stop. **[1]**

**(c)** The driver’s reaction time is 0.70 s. Determine the total stopping distance. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $v^2 = u^2 + 2as \Rightarrow 0 = 625 + 80a$ (✓) $a = -7.8$ m s⁻² ✓

**(b)** $t = \dfrac{25}{7.8} = 3.2$ s ✓

**(c)** Thinking distance $25\times0.70 = 17.5$ m ✓; total $= 57.5 \approx 58$ m ✓
